        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by freeing the workqueues in the `dlm_lowcomms_stop()` function before cleaning up the queued works, leading to an attempt to access already freed memory in the `free_conn()` function when it tried to cancel those queued works. This access to freed memory resulted in potential race conditions and undefined behavior.
        
        Commit message:
        dlm: free workqueues after the connections

After backporting commit ee44b4bc054a ("dlm: use sctp 1-to-1 API")
series to a kernel with an older workqueue which didn't use RCU yet, it
was noticed that we are freeing the workqueues in dlm_lowcomms_stop()
too early as free_conn() will try to access that memory for canceling
the queued works if any.

This issue was introduced by commit 0d737a8cfd83 as before it such
attempt to cancel the queued works wasn't performed, so the issue was
not present.

This patch fixes it by simply inverting the free order.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 0d737a8cfd83 ("dlm: fix race while closing connections")
Signed-off-by: Marcelo Ricardo Leitner <marcelo.leitner@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David Teigland <teigland@redhat.com>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/fs/dlm/lowcomms.c b/fs/dlm/lowcomms.c
index 963016c8f3d1..609998de533e 100644
--- a/fs/dlm/lowcomms.c
+++ b/fs/dlm/lowcomms.c
@@ -1656,16 +1656,12 @@ void dlm_lowcomms_stop(void)
 	mutex_lock(&connections_lock);
 	dlm_allow_conn = 0;
 	foreach_conn(stop_conn);
+	clean_writequeues();
+	foreach_conn(free_conn);
 	mutex_unlock(&connections_lock);
 
 	work_stop();
 
-	mutex_lock(&connections_lock);
-	clean_writequeues();
-
-	foreach_conn(free_conn);
-
-	mutex_unlock(&connections_lock);
 	kmem_cache_destroy(con_cache);
 }

Here is the commit message:
dlm: free workqueues after the connections

After backporting commit ee44b4bc054a ("dlm: use sctp 1-to-1 API")
series to a kernel with an older workqueue which didn't use RCU yet, it
was noticed that we are freeing the workqueues in dlm_lowcomms_stop()
too early as free_conn() will try to access that memory for canceling
the queued works if any.

This issue was introduced by commit 0d737a8cfd83 as before it such
attempt to cancel the queued works wasn't performed, so the issue was
not present.

This patch fixes it by simply inverting the free order.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 0d737a8cfd83 ("dlm: fix race while closing connections")
Signed-off-by: Marcelo Ricardo Leitner <marcelo.leitner@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David Teigland <teigland@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by freeing the workqueues in the `dlm_lowcomms_stop()` function before cleaning up the queued works, leading to an attempt to access already freed memory in the `free_conn()` function when it tried to cancel those queued works. This access to freed memory resulted in potential race conditions and undefined behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
 void dlm_lowcomms_stop(void)
 {
 	/* Set all the flags to prevent any
 	   socket activity.
 	*/
 	mutex_lock(&connections_lock);
 	dlm_allow_conn = 0;
 	foreach_conn(stop_conn);
+	clean_writequeues();
+	foreach_conn(free_conn);
 	mutex_unlock(&connections_lock);
 
 	work_stop();
 
-	mutex_lock(&connections_lock);
-	clean_writequeues();
-
-	foreach_conn(free_conn);
-
-	mutex_unlock(&connections_lock);
 	kmem_cache_destroy(con_cache);
 }


The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
clean_writequeues();
foreach_conn(free_conn);
```
Reason:
By moving the `clean_writequeues();` and `foreach_conn(free_conn);` statements before the `work_stop();` function, the queued works are properly cleaned up and canceled before the workqueues are freed. This ensures that there are no attempts to access freed memory, thus preventing the race conditions and undefined behavior.
